it'll be a hard sell for Persona at the moment. Generally, especially this
year, decisions have leaned more toward building in-house rather than
buying. The ML labeling/annotation pipelines are pretty core flows at
Persona and most of our pipelines focus on labeling/annotating
ids/documents.

I'm mentioning all of this to give you a heads up on what to expect.

That all being said, vendors are often integrated because fires are burning
and it's the quickest way to solve the immediate problem at hand. I can't
predict when a fire will happen. So I can still take the call and keep the
product in mind in case a need arises.

subject: Re: Encord Annotation Persona Requirements
text:
*--SecureDelivery—*

Hi Will,

This package contains the current state workflows in place today.

A few call-outs:

  1.
Today, team members must be notified manually which project to work on. Prioritization of what is in the queue is a need. A ‘get next’ functionality to streamline provider workflow would be ideal.
  2.
The single pane of glass must include contextual insights if there are clarifying questions about an question set - this is standard to our CAVA Hub experience today which is ingesting information the same as Encord will (no API). I have included an example of this today.
  3.
Training within the tool is desired so they can add things like the PPT trainings to support annotation processes.
  4.
Metadata about the case will need to be viewable including patient age, CPT code and date of submission (this is relevant as multiple CPT codes are annotated in the same case). I have included an example of this today.
  5.
They added a pick list for reasons criteria not met to the workflow (to standardize response) I have included this list.
     *
This also makes me believe a pick list for reason for disagreement could be valuable vs simple open field. I’d love your POV on this.

I imagine we complete a workflow review with the clinical team after a prototype is ready? This seems like the right point to ensure we are showing them how we have met the requirements and are modeling after current state while creating room for feedback/adjustments. Does that seem like the right approach or do you want to meet before then for Q&A with the team on workflow?

Thanks,
Kaylene
